test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 28 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The volume of a cylinder is 5500 m³. Find its diameter of base if the height of the cylinder is 70 m. [Use pi = (22)/(7)]
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Volume of Cylinder** formula: **Volume = πr²h**

Substitute values: 5500 = (22/7) × r² × 70

Simplify: 5500 = 220 × r²

⇒ r² = 25 ⇒ Radius (r) = 5 m

Diameter (d) = 2 × Radius = 2 × 5 = 10 m

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume of the **cylinder** (V) = 5500 m³

Height of the **cylinder** (h) = 70 m

Value of π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

**Volume (V) = π × r² × h**

**Diameter (d) = 2 × r**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff7f42fdff01d0d37e2cab89b6c83d4ea6cbb99aa4cfa22fa38ed3a14d2de4f4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = πr²h

⇒ 5500 = (22/7) × r² × 70

⇒ 5500 = 22 × r² × (70 ÷ 7)

⇒ 5500 = 22 × r² × 10

⇒ 5500 = 220 × r²

⇒ r² = 5500 ÷ 220

⇒ r² = 25

⇒ r = √25 = 5 m

⇒ Diameter (d) = 2 × 5

⇒ Diameter = 10 m

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the curved surface of a **cylinder** is given by the formula **2πrh**.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The total surface area including the top and bottom circular bases is **2πr(h + r)**.

Area of Base

The **base area** of a cylinder is circular and is calculated as **πr²**.

Volume of Cone

The volume of a **cone** with the same base radius and height is **(1/3)πr²h**, which is one-third the volume of the cylinder.</p
